newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZDB sees 23 pct lift in dairy exports this season.
newsitem.headline: NZDB sees 23 pct lift in dairy exports this season.

text.p: The New Zealand Dairy Board said on Friday a 10 percent increase in milk production and anticipated sales from stocks of 130,000 tonnes will see this season's dairy exports rise by 23 percent, or 240,000 tonnes.

"To do this we have had to capture increased market share. On a global basis, the New Zealand Dairy Board has around 24 percent of the accessible world dairy trade. It has been an excellent and commendable effort," Board chairman Sir Dryden Spring said.

Spring also said that had the New Zealand dollar not appreciated over the past three years, the board's payout this season would have been NZ$3.90 cents/kkg milksolids, rather than the $3.15 - $3.20 currently forecast.
He said the cumulative erosion of payout over that time, net of any hedging activities, was $1.17 cents/kg.
Spring said the board, through its hedging programmes, had managed to "claw back" around one third of the cost of the currency's appreciation.

He said the present best estimate of 1997/98 payout prospects was a return slightly down on this year's result, but that recent events had been more encouraging, with a softer New Zealand dollar and modest prospects of a firmer market later in the year.
